correctness.rationale: For an injective vertex order on the unfilled friendship graph, the descending link is discrete; a pairing is produced exactly when there is one earlier neighbor. A petal entirely before the hub produces its one internal arrow, a petal entirely after the hub its first outer-to-hub arrow, and a split petal no outer arrow. Every selection from the four-point petal factors is realized by placing all internal-choice petals entirely before the hub and the rest after it, with the chosen orientations; the downward closure gives the entire join. A hub-origin arrow forces exactly one earlier outer vertex, so its petal supplies no other pair and all other petals have the two outer-to-hub choices. These choices are all realized and give two cones per petal. Distinct apices never occur together, so the intersection at each attachment is the base, the join of n-1 two-point sets, an S^(n-2). Its inclusion is null because it lies in the cone given by any point of the omitted four-point factor. The simplicial inclusion is a cofibration, so its mapping cone wedges on the suspension S^(n-1), including the two-point base at n=2. The core join has 3^n spheres (iteratively join with four points, i.e. attach four cones along the previous join). Counting faces of the core and faces containing exactly one exceptional apex proves the polynomial. For n=1 every vertex order produces one pair, all six occur, and the six isolated vertices give 1+6t.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration checks only n≤3, and the frozen mod-two computations only the listed finite cases. Neither computation is used as an integral homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: A distinct published record, Resultary c88f401c5072, demonstrably covers both principal claims for the identical full complex, including the same defining vertex-order rule, the wedge theorem and the complete face data. It also displays the same core join and exceptional cone decomposition. Adding the empty-face term to that record's exact face vector is not distinct mathematical content. The n=1 wedge is already in Knudson–Owens–White. No separate original remainder was identified. This is an equivalent-coverage decision: the exact matching catalogue record's publication field is later than the frozen record, and the comparison does not assert that the later record anticipated this one, assign priority, or infer how either record was produced.
residual_risks: The relationship and priority between the two exact matching Resultary records are unresolved; there is no inference of derivation or independence.

value.rationale: As mathematics, the uniform integral homotopy and complete face enumeration of a natural one-vertex amalgamation family address a structural question not answered by a disjoint-union join law. The explicit cones explain the effect of the common hub, and the contrast with the ordinary edge-matching complex on the same graphs is substantive. This value does not negate equivalent coverage of the actual result.
